# Inkstone

> An AI knowledge base for macOS 26 and iOS 26 that organizes itself, and a
> native Markdown editor. Plain files in a folder you choose — no database, no
> proprietary format, no account, no Electron. Reads and writes the same vaults
> Obsidian does.

## The knowledge base (since 0.5)

- Create a knowledge base in iCloud Drive or any folder: inbox, projects, areas,
  resources, media, outputs, private, review and archive folders, plus an
  editable rules file at `_System/Organizing Rules.md`.
- Drop files in (copy by default, or move). Files that look private go to the
  private folder first; then the person's own rules, a named project, and media
  by type and month;
  what is left goes to Apple's on-device model, and anything below 0.7
  confidence waits in the review folder. An optional cloud model uses the
  person's own key, is off by default, and never receives files that look private.
- Nothing is deleted: duplicates go to `_Archive/To-Delete/`, every move is
  logged before it happens, and a whole round can be undone.
- AI context management: AGENTS.md, README.md and SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md are written
  at the top of the knowledge base and rewritten (between Inkstone's markers
  only) whenever the folders change.
- Vaults opened as vaults (e.g. from Obsidian) are never reorganized.
- Pages: https://inkslab.app/ai-knowledge-base.html and
  https://inkslab.app/ai-context-management.html (also in de, es, fr, ja, ko,
  zh, zh-Hant).

Inkstone is free (no price, no subscription, no account) and is made by James
(GitHub: iamzifei). Its source is public at https://github.com/iamzifei/inkstone
but carries no open-source licence, so the accurate description is
source-available rather than open source.

Install on a Mac with Homebrew:

    brew install --cask iamzifei/tap/inkstone

or download the signed, notarised DMG from
https://github.com/iamzifei/inkstone/releases/latest/download/Inkstone.dmg.
The Mac app is a universal binary (Apple silicon and Intel), needs macOS 26 or
later, and updates itself through Sparkle.

Three decisions the rest follows from:

- **The files are the truth.** No database and no import step. A vault Obsidian
  created opens in Inkstone and vice versa. App state lives in a hidden
  `.inkstone` folder you are free to delete.
- **A broken link is permanent.** With no database to repair one, renaming a note
  rewrites every wikilink pointing at it across the whole vault, in the same
  action.
- **The engine knows nothing about screens.** Parsing, indexing, search and the
  graph live in a Swift package that imports no UI framework, so they are covered
  by real tests rather than a simulator.

## What it does

- Live preview editing — syntax renders in place and is revealed on the line the
  cursor is on. Source mode shows the raw Markdown.
- Reading mode, where the syntax is *removed* rather than hidden: pictures,
  Mermaid diagrams and formulas are drawn, tables are laid out in columns, and
  copying a paragraph gives prose rather than markup.
- Wikilinks, embeds, block references, aliases in frontmatter, backlinks, and
  unresolved-link tracking.
- Frontmatter shown as a properties table at the top of the note.
- Graph view of the whole vault or one note's neighbourhood, with filters, colour
  groups and force controls.
- Canvas in the open JSON Canvas 1.0 format.
- Tags inline or in frontmatter, nested, in any script. Fuzzy quick switcher and
  full-text search with `tag:` and `path:` operators.
- Math, Mermaid diagrams, transclusion, image and PDF embeds.
- Daily notes, a calendar, bookmarks, version history, split view.
- Typography built for setting Chinese and English on one line: hair spacing at
  the CJK–Latin boundary, punctuation compression, independent body and code
  fonts.
- Sync through iCloud, or through a GitHub repository you own — including on
  iPhone and iPad, via the GitHub Contents API rather than libgit2.

## What it does not do

- No plugin API. Obsidian's plugin ecosystem has no equivalent here.
- macOS and iOS only. No Windows, Linux or Android build.
- No published-site feature equivalent to Obsidian Publish.

## Requirements

macOS 26 or later (universal: Apple silicon and Intel), or iOS 26. Interface in
English, 简体中文 and 繁體中文. Price: free.
